First-order ¹H stick patterns are drawn only when the literature reports both multiplicity and J. The ¹H splitting is illustrated at a nominal 500 MHz reference scale; this is not a lineshape calculation or an integral measurement. Unresolved patterns are not invented. ¹³C peaks represent published shifts, typically proton-decoupled.

Sources and criteria

Fulmer et al. · Organometallics (2010) — ¹H and ¹³C tables in 12 deuterated solvents.

Babij et al. · Org. Process Res. Dev. (2016) — 48 process solvents in 6 deuterated media; when a compound is already in Fulmer, the 2010 values are kept separate rather than merged.

Gottlieb et al. · J. Org. Chem. (1997) — historical reference, not loaded in duplicate.

The ranking sorts first by the number of matched signals, then by agreement relative to the selected tolerances. It does not estimate identity probabilities. OH peaks, OD isotopomers, and shifts that depend strongly on concentration or temperature require extra caution.
